printers.name: Aries
notes: Open-frame Ender-5-style Cartesian cube, mapped to the conservative bedslinger tuning bucket
Official Voxelab manual: FDM, 200x200x200mm, 0.4mm standard nozzle, 1.75mm PLA/ABS/PETG, 250C nozzle max, 110C bed max, <=180mm/s
Glass build plate; single 0.4mm nozzle (other sizes not listed in the manual)
max_acceleration 5000 is a conservative app-side cap (no manufacturer acceleration figure is published by Voxelab) - not a claimed manufacturer maximum

Ultrabase coated-glass bed

printers.name: 2.0 A350
notes: Request was for "Snapmaker 2" (no sub-model). Added as the A350 — the flagship/largest Snapmaker 2.0 — as the conservative representative: it has the LOWEST max bed temp of the 2.0 line (A350 80C < A250 100C < A150 ~100C), so its profile is the safe default. A150/A250 owners get the same nozzle/motion limits and a safe (lower) bed cap.
Snapmaker 2.0: lead-screw-driven 3-in-1 modular Cartesian (FDM + laser + CNC); mapped to the conservative bedslinger motion bucket. Open-frame by default (enclosure is a separate accessory).
Official spec: FDM, 0.4mm direct-drive hot end, 275C max nozzle, 80C max bed (A350 hardware limit), single-extrusion build volume ~320x335x310mm.

max_speed 120 and max_acceleration 3000 are from Snapmaker's official firmware motion config (Snapmaker/Snapmaker2-Controller Marlin Configuration.h: DEFAULT_MAX_FEEDRATE X/Y=120 mm/s, DEFAULT_MAX_ACCELERATION X/Y=3000 mm/s2). Real-world print speed is ~60mm/s due to lead-screw kinematics.

printers.name: Creator 5 Pro
notes: Enclosed CoreXY with 4 independent direct-drive toolheads (FlashSwap tool-changing) — mapped to the multi_color_systems 'toolchanger' tier.
Active heated chamber up to 65C; HEPA13 + activated-carbon filtration; built-in 1280x720 camera.
Official spec: FDM, 256x256x256mm, 320C max nozzle, 120C max bed, 65C max chamber, PEI textured flexible steel plate, nozzles 0.25/0.4/0.6/0.8mm.

max_speed 300 mm/s is FlashForge's published spec-table value (flashforge.com + flashforge.com.hk). Marketing/reviews cite '600 mm/s' as a travel/peak figure, not steady print speed; the conservative spec-table 300 is used.

printers.name: U1
notes: Snapmaker U1: CoreXY toolchanger with 4 independent direct-drive print heads (SnapSwap system, 5-second toolchange). Multi-color via toolchanger reduces filament waste by up to 80% versus conventional single-nozzle systems; the U1 can still build a small prime/wiping tower during color changes. FDM only (dedicated 3D printer, not modular 3-in-1 like the 2.0 series).

Specs confirmed from manufacturer pages: 300°C nozzle, 100°C bed, 500mm/s, 20000mm/s² accel, CoreXY, direct-drive toolchanger (https://www.snapmaker.com/snapmaker-u1/specs); compatible 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8mm U1 hot ends (https://shop.snapmaker.com/products/hot-end-for-snapmaker-u1).
Series_group “U Series” owner-approved; available_plates: textured_pei confirmed from manufacturer spec page (Flexible Steel Sheet with PEI Surface).

printers.name: Ender-3 S1
notes: Open-frame Ender Series bed-slinger — 220×220×270mm build volume, dual Z-axis lead screws, not suitable for ABS/ASA/PA/PC without enclosure modification

Sprite dual-gear direct extruder, CR-Touch 16-point auto bed leveling; PC-coated spring steel plate standard, tempered glass and PEI sold separately — https://www.creality3dofficial.com/products/ender-3-s1-direct-drive-3d-printer

max_acceleration 500mm/s2 (X/Y) is Creality's official shipped firmware default, not an app-side cap — Ender-3S1/Marlin/Configuration.h DEFAULT_MAX_ACCELERATION: https://github.com/CrealityOfficial/Ender-3S1/blob/main/Marlin/Configuration.h
No camera, no LiDAR, single extruder (no multi-color system) per official spec page

printers.name: Adventurer 3
notes: Discontinued (~2019) entry-level fully-enclosed FDM printer — 150x150x150mm build volume, 45dB ultra-quiet operation, WiFi/FlashCloud remote control (https://au.flashforge.com/blogs/news/is-the-adventurer-3-still-any-good-in-2025)

extruder_type=bowden, max_nozzle_temp=240C, max_bed_temp=100C, available_nozzle_sizes=[0.4], and has_camera=true confirmed via the official FlashForge Adventurer 3 User Guide (https://en.fss.flashforge.com/10000/software/2ff1e48618315861cfee296866c0392a.pdf) — Reference table p.07, Preheat Setting p.16, Chapter 2.5 Camera User Manual; Q&A p.46 describes unclogging via the guide-tube air-tube-joint, consistent with a Bowden feed path

multi_color_systems=[] confirmed via the same User Guide — Chapter 1 Terms defines a single 'Extruder' (integral device on X-Axis, singular) and the Components diagram (1.1) shows one nozzle/filament intake/filament cartridge slot; no multi-material, IDEX, or toolchanging system is mentioned anywhere in the manual
series=bedslinger and available_plates=[textured_pei, smooth_glass] per owner attestation (issue #27) — see field-level owner-attested provenance

max_acceleration=400mm/s² is a conservative app-side cap, not a manufacturer spec — no manufacturer source (official product page, user manual, or FlashForge wiki) publishes an acceleration figure for this legacy 2019 model, and neither reseller listings nor independent community reviews do either; capped at the lowest bedslinger-bucket sibling already shipped (anycubic mega_x, 400mm/s², a comparably legacy 100mm/s Bowden bedslinger)

printers.name: Ender-3 S1 Pro
notes: Open-frame Ender Series bed-slinger — 220×220×270mm build volume, Sprite full-metal dual-gear direct extruder (80N extrusion force) — https://www.creality.com/products/creality-ender-3-s1-pro-fdm-3d-printer
PEI spring steel build plate standard (vs PC spring steel on base Ender-3 S1); CR-Touch 16-point auto bed leveling — https://www.creality.com/blog/the-differences-of-ender-3-s1-ender-3-s1-plus

max_speed=150mm/s: manufacturer-vs-manufacturer conflict resolved by the specification-grade-outranks-marketing-copy ladder (docs/runbooks/printer-addition-protocol.md). Official User Manual V1.4 Device Specifications table (Shenzhen Creality 3D Technology Co., Ltd, page 12/14) states 'Printing Speed: Up to 150 mm/s, recommended 50 mm/s' — a specification table. store.creality.com Canada product-page TITLE states 'max speed 160mm/s' with no supporting spec table (marketing copy only, confirmed by direct fetch). Rung 1 applies: spec-grade value taken as confirmed. Matches shipped sibling ender_3_s1 (150mm/s). Sources: https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/B1VeQWylTYL.pdf (manual, spec table) and https://store.creality.com/ca/products/ender-3-s1-pro-3d-printer (title-only, marketing copy).

max_acceleration 500mm/s2 (X/Y) is Creality's official shipped firmware default, not an app-side cap — Ender-3S1/Marlin/Configuration.h DEFAULT_MAX_ACCELERATION (s1_pro_plus branch, ENDER_3S1_PRO target): https://github.com/CrealityOfficial/Ender-3S1/blob/s1_pro_plus/Marlin/Configuration.h

No camera, no LiDAR, single extruder (no multi-color system) per official User Manual V1.4 (Device Specifications table + Accessory Kit Items list, silent on all three) — https://www.creality.com/products/creality-ender-3-s1-pro-fdm-3d-printer
